title: AI-optimized magnetic nanobiocatalyst enables recyclable citrulline production
summary: A neural-network-assisted optimization selected a magnetic-nanoparticle formulation of arginine deiminase for citrulline production. The prepared catalyst achieved 70.0% activity recovery, near the predicted 71.18%, and 81.4% immobilization efficiency. It retained approximately 64% activity after 40 days at 4 °C, exceeded 74% after seven reuse cycles, and converted 99.1% of arginine to citrulline. These are laboratory formulation results; model training used only 30 observations and industrial or continuous-flow performance remains untested.
ai_technology: Hybrid Whale Optimization–artificial neural network (WO-ANN) for immobilization-condition optimization

evidence.tested: Thirty designed experiments informed WO-ANN optimization; the selected conditions were experimentally tested (70.0% activity recovery vs predicted 71.18%, 81.4% immobilization efficiency). The immobilized enzyme retained about 64% activity after 40 days at 4 °C, was reused for seven cycles and achieved 99.1% L-arginine to L-citrulline conversion.
evidence.unknown: Continuous-flow performance, process scale-up and industrial operating outcomes are not established. The ANN was trained on only 30 design observations (21/4/5 train/validation/test); generalization beyond the tested factor ranges remains uncertain.
evidence.ai_role: A feed-forward neural network predicts activity recovery from four formulation variables; Whale Optimization uses the model to select immobilization conditions, which are then tested experimentally.

source_review.scope: Source-provenanced primary publisher HTML abstract, WO-ANN methods, optimized formulation tests, stability/reuse/conversion results, prior-formulation comparison, affiliations and publication history. Full PDF was available but independent reading used HTML.
